# lumos_entitlement_provisioning_workflow (Resource)

EntitlementProvisioningWorkflow Resource

This resource binds an existing `lumos_workflow` to a slot on a entitlement. It does
not create the workflow itself — set `workflow_id` to the id of a workflow that
already exists.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "lumos_entitlement_provisioning_workflow" "my_entitlementprovisioningworkflow" {
  entitlement_uuid = "...my_entitlement_uuid..."
  workflow_id      = "...my_workflow_id..."
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `entitlement_uuid` (String) Requires replacement if changed.
- `workflow_id` (String) UUID of the workflow to associate.

### Read-Only

- `app_id` (String) UUID of the app this Workflow belongs to, if associated.
- `description` (String) A description of this Workflow.
- `id` (String) A UUID identifying this Workflow.
- `name` (String) A name for this Workflow.
- `steps` (Attributes List) The ordered steps of the workflow. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--steps))
- `type` (String) The kind of workflow.

### Nested Schema for `steps`

Read-Only:

- `inputs` (Attributes) The configured inputs for this step. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--steps--inputs))
- `name` (String) Server-derived human-readable name for this step. Read-only.
- `step` (String) Identifier (catalogue slug) for the step to execute.

## Destroy behavior

~> **Destroying this resource does not unbind the workflow.**

The API exposes no unbind operation for this slot — only `GET` and `PUT` on
`/v1/entitlements/{entitlement_uuid}/provisioning-workflow`. `terraform destroy` therefore removes the
resource from Terraform state while the entitlement keeps the workflow bound in
Lumos. Nothing is called against the API.

To change the binding, set `workflow_id` to a different workflow and apply; the
`PUT` overwrites the slot in place. Changing `entitlement_uuid` instead replaces the
resource, because a binding belongs to exactly one entitlement.

## Import

Import addresses the binding by its owning entitlement, not by the workflow:

```shell
terraform import lumos_entitlement_provisioning_workflow.example "<entitlement_uuid>"
```

-> **Expect one no-op update on the first plan after an import.** `workflow_id`
is write-only — the API returns the bound workflow under `id`, never echoing
back the `workflow_id` that was sent — so an imported binding has `workflow_id`
null in state. The first plan proposes null -> your configured value and applies
a `PUT` that rebinds the workflow already bound. It is idempotent and changes
nothing. Read `id` after importing to see which workflow is currently bound.
